- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (e.g., >0.5) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct.
- Underestimate prices during negative sentiment periods (sentiment < 0.3) — model is overly optimistic or fails to recognize bearish momentum.
- When sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (0.0–0.3), model often overreacts to recent highs, leading to premature peaks.
- Mean reversion bias: model frequently fails to recognize that prices revert to recent 10–15 day averages after sharp moves, especially in high-sentiment periods.
- Lagged corrections: model often delays downward corrections after negative sentiment spikes — true price drops occur faster than forecasted.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early cycles (e.g., 2025-06-16) when sentiment is high, but underperform in later cycles (e.g., 2025-06-19) when sentiment is low or neutral.
- Sentiment-driven bias: if sentiment is consistently positive, model overweights momentum; if sentiment is negative, model underweights risk — both lead to systematic directional errors.
